red signboard front face with 국밥 lettering

answer.evidence: The top cap spans rows 1-7. Its width grows from 12 at row 1 to 16 at rows 2-6, with a white highlight at rows 2-4, so it overhangs the body. It ends in a darker front-edge line at row 7 (L=71), and the dark outline at row 8 acts as a 1-row eave shadow. Below it the red board is a front face of about 22 rows (rows 8-30, width 14) carrying the cream lettering. No isometric side face is drawn. The cap is a visible horizontal top surface above a tall front face, so this is three-quarter rather than a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical red signboard with a cream '국밥' glyph and a dark red-brown outline. The outline is visibly tinted (0% near-neutral dark edges, same as all references), so it reads as dark_material_tone, not a black sticker line. It has 10 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. It is a narrower, simpler piece than the vending machine and kiosk, which carry more panel detail, buttons and highlights. That makes it somewhat lower in density than the richest references, but it is within the range of the shipped modern_city art and is not shallow.

The cap's width profile (8, 12, 16, then 14) is not a true ellipse, so I rely on evidence (a) rather than (b). The call is borderline because the cap is only 6 rows and is drawn nearly flat.
